title: Quarterly scenario planning: hosted API + model catalog convergence
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures the scenario-driven quarterly roadmap plan for Hosted API + Model Catalog. Goal is to produce a prioritized set of initiatives, a staged rollout plan, and gating criteria that align with Q2 OKRs (latency cost targets, model coverage, and reliability). The output will be a published playbook for engineering/design/infra that includes target milestones, risk mitigations, and dependencies for Dedicated and Private customers. This differs from prior artifacts by explicitly modeling 3 usage scenarios (high-throughput low-latency, cost-sensitive batch embeddings, and enterprise isolated deployments) and mapping model variants and runtime optimizations to each scenario.
objectives: O1: Reduce median generation latency for common small prompt workloads by 15% across hosted endpoints
O2: Add and certify 6 new model variants in the catalog including two quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads
O3: Define canary + rollback playbook for model swaps with <0.5% customer error impact target
O4: Create scenario-based config templates (throughput, latency, cost) for customers to adopt hosted/dedicated/private
success_metrics: Metric 1: Median P50 latency decrease of 15% for 128-token prompts on standard-hosted endpoints
Metric 2: 6 model variants published with perf profiles and eval pass rates >90% on regression suite
Metric 3: Canary runbook validated in 3 internal experiments with automatic rollback triggered correctly
Metric 4: 3 scenario templates shipped and adopted by at least 5 pilot customers
milestones: M1: Scenario definitions and customer archetypes finalized (2026-02-22)
M2: Candidate model list and quantization plan confirmed with Applied ML (2026-03-05)
M3: Runtime config recommendations (batching/KV/cache) for scenarios documented (2026-03-18)
M4: Canary playbook and observability dashboards implemented (2026-03-25)
M5: Pilot rollouts with two customers and feedback loop (2026-03-31)
M6: Publish public Hosted API + Model Catalog scenario playbook (2026-04-01)
risks: R1: Model onboarding delays due to unexpected eval regressions
R2: Runtime kernel/quantization regressions leading to higher latency for some sequences
R3: Canary thresholds too tight or too loose, causing false positives/negatives
R4: Cross-team bandwidth conflicts during March code freeze windows
mitigation_plan: For R1: Prioritize automated regression fixes and plan a contingency model variant that is already verified
For R2: Schedule extra kernel-validation time with Runtime Eng and add synthetic perf tests to CI
For R3: Run two staged canaries (internal traffic, then opt-in small customer cohort) before broad rollout
For R4: Coordinate with Eng leads to reserve a three-day window for model rollout work and embargo other non-critical merges
decisions: D1: Adopt scenario templates rather than per-customer bespoke configs to accelerate onboarding
D2: Require all new catalog models to have a quantized or cost-optimized variant unless technically infeasible
D3: Use existing rollout infra (canary + automatic fallback) for model swaps; build lightweight guardrails rather than heavy orchestration
tasks: T1: Run workload characterization for top 20 hosted API customers (owner: Diego Morales) - due 2026-02-26
T2: Produce model candidate matrix with eval pass/fail and perf profiles (owner: Maya Chen) - due 2026-03-05
T3: Draft runtime recommendation doc and scenario config templates (owner: Jonah Erickson + Runtime Eng) - due 2026-03-12
T4: Instrument dashboards for canary metrics and error budget tracking (owner: Observability team) - due 2026-03-20
T5: Run two internal canary experiments and capture playbook steps (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-25
T6: Coordinate pilot customer signups and feedback sessions (owner: Customer Success) - due 2026-03-31
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Playbook published with scenario templates, model matrix, rollout runbook, and dashboard links
AC2: At least two internal canary runs completed and results documented
AC3: 6 model variants added to catalog with perf profiles and quantized alternatives where applicable
AC4: Risk register and rollback procedures validated by SRE
notes: This artifact should be used as the canonical reference for Q2 hosted API + model catalog alignment. It intentionally focuses on scenario-driven trade-offs to help Sales/CS pick configurations and for engineering to prioritize optimizations. Expect follow-up tickets scoped into ENG and DES for implementation work.
